learning.learning_goal: Understand that 'how many more' asks for the gap between two amounts.
learning.big_idea: Comparison means finding the gap between two amounts.

screens.label: Lesson 001
screens.title: How many more?
screens.body: Comparison means finding the gap between two amounts.

screens.label: Misconception
screens.title: Does more always mean add?
screens.prompt: Ava has 14 stickers. Luis has 8. How many more stickers does Ava have?

choices.text: 6, because the question asks for the gap
choices.feedback: The word more describes a comparison here, so find the gap.

hints: The question does not ask how many stickers they have altogether.
Compare 14 with 8 and find what is unmatched.

visual.message: Both rows start in the same place. Which row goes farther?

screens.label: Discover
screens.title: What do the glowing blocks show?

visual.message: The extra blocks show how much farther the top row goes.

choices.feedback: The glowing blocks show the gap.

hints: Look at the two rows side by side.
Look for the blocks that do not have a match.
Only count the blocks that do not have a match.

screens.label: Language
screens.title: Different words. Same gap.

visual.message: These phrases all point to the same relationship.

screens.guidance: Some words can be tricky. First ask: are we putting groups together, or comparing them?

screens.label: Remember
screens.title: Compare? Find the gap.
screens.body: When two amounts are being compared, more tells you which amount is larger—not automatically to add.

screens.label: Symbol
screens.title: What equation measures the gap?

visual.message: The top row goes farther. Which equation measures that gap?

choices.feedback: Start with the larger amount and subtract the smaller amount.

hints: The equation should measure what is extra.
Start with 15 because it is the larger group.

visual.message: The equation confirms what the visual showed.

screens.label: Guided practice
screens.title: Find the unmatched shells.

visual.message: Eleven shells are matched with seven. Count only the unmatched shells.

choices.feedback: Four shells are unmatched, so 11 is 4 more than 7.

hints: Match the first seven shells in each row.

screens.label: Independent practice
screens.title: Solve without the model.
screens.prompt: Nia read 16 pages. Theo read 9 pages. How many more pages did Nia read?
hints: Decide whether the question asks for a total or a comparison.
Subtract the smaller amount from the larger amount.

screens.label: Recall
screens.title: What should you remember?
screens.prompt: When a problem asks how many more one amount is than another, what should you find?

choices.feedback: How many more asks for the gap between the amounts.

hints: Recall the memory hook: Compare? Find the gap.

screens.label: Transfer
screens.title: Use the idea in a new setting.
screens.prompt: A blue notebook costs $18 and a red notebook costs $11. How much more does the blue notebook cost?

choices.feedback: $18 − $11 = $7, so the blue notebook costs $7 more.

hints: The context changed, but the question still asks for a gap.

screens.label: Reflect
screens.title: What did you discover?
screens.prompt: Choose the statement that explains the idea.

choices.text: Subtraction can measure the gap between two amounts.
The word more always means add.

hints: Think about what the blocks showed.

screens.title: You measured the gap.
screens.body: You connected the visual, the words, and the equation.
